contents.title: Quiz Diagnostic 1ere Anglais - Serie 34
contents.subject: Anglais
contents.description: Diagnostic Anglais 1ere : Les formes du futur

questions.question: Choose the correct future form: 'Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain.'
'I will call you back in five minutes' expresses a spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking.
Quelle forme du futur utiliser et pourquoi ? 'I've already bought the tickets. We ___ (see) the concert next Saturday.'
Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect?
choices: By next year, she will finish her degree.
By next year, she will have finished her degree.
By next year, she is going to finish her degree.
By next year, she has finished her degree.

questions.question: The present continuous can be used to talk about fixed, arranged plans in the near future.
Complète avec will ou going to et justifie : 'A: The phone is ringing. B: Don't worry, I ___ answer it.'
Choose the correct future form: 'By the time you arrive, I ___ cooking dinner.'
'Shall' is commonly used in American English to express future actions.

exercisenotion.description: Will s'utilise pour : (1) une décision prise au moment où l'on parle : 'I'll have the salad.' (2) une promesse : 'I will help you.' (3) une prédiction basée sur une opinion : 'I think it will rain.' (4) des faits futurs certains : 'She will be 18 next month.'

exercisenotion.notion: Going to – intention planifiée, prédiction basée sur des indices
exercisenotion.description: Be going to s'utilise pour : (1) une intention ou un plan décidé à l'avance : 'I'm going to study medicine.' (2) une prédiction basée sur des indices visibles maintenant : 'Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.' La différence avec 'will' : going to = déjà décidé, will = décision spontanée.

exercisenotion.notion: Future Perfect – action accomplie avant un moment futur
exercisenotion.description: Le future perfect (will have + past participle) exprime une action qui sera terminée avant un moment précis dans le futur. Marqueurs : by, by the time, before. Ex : 'By 2030, scientists will have found a cure.' / 'I will have finished this report by 5pm.'
